## Syntax

A wikilink is a page name in double brackets:

`[[Getting Started]]`

Optional pieces can be added:

- **Display text**: `[[Getting Started|the setup guide]]` renders as a link
  reading "the setup guide".
- **Heading link**: `[[Getting Started#5. Render]]` links to the
  `## 5. Render` heading within that page. Combine with display text:
  `[[Getting Started#5. Render|the render step]]`.
- **Case insensitivity**: matching against the registry ignores case, so
  `[[getting STARTED]]` resolves the same as the canonical form.

## How targets resolve to pages

A pre-render pass scans every page in the project once, before any page
renders, and builds a registry of link targets. Each page contributes:

- its `title:` frontmatter (or its folder-path identifier, if no title is
  set — see below)
- its folder-path identifier: the bare filename stem, with folder and
  extension stripped, for a normal page — but for an `index.qmd`, that's the
  name of the folder it's *in*, not the word "index". A page at
  `page1/index.qmd` is a folder note, the same way Obsidian's folder-note
  plugins and Quartz treat it: it *is* `page1`, so `[[page1]]` resolves to
  it directly. The bare word `index` itself is never a usable target — every
  folder's `index.qmd` would otherwise "collide" on it, which isn't a real
  ambiguity — except for the project's own top-level `index.qmd`, the one
  page where "index" is unique by construction.
- progressively longer folder-qualified forms of both the above: `[[api]]`,
  and if that's ambiguous, `[[docs/api]]`, `[[project/docs/api]]`, and so on
  up to the page's full path. This is also how an explicit `index` suffix
  keeps working if you'd rather spell it out: `[[page1/index]]` resolves the
  same page as `[[page1]]`.
- each name listed under `also-known-as:` in its frontmatter (a single
  string or a list of strings) — these are exact-match only, not
  folder-qualified, since they're already a deliberately-chosen unique name.

All of these are lowercased before being stored, which is what makes lookups
case-insensitive.

Note that `also-known-as:` is a quarto-graph-specific key, distinct from
Quarto's built-in `aliases:` (which is for redirect URLs, not link
resolution).

For example, [[Getting Started]] has this frontmatter:

```yaml
---
title: Getting Started
---
```

which registers it under both `Getting Started` (title) and
`getting-started` (stem). Adding an `also-known-as:` list would register
more names for the same page:

```yaml
---
title: Getting Started
also-known-as:
  - Setup
  - Installation
---
```

After that, `[[Setup]]` and `[[Installation]]` would resolve to this same
page too.

Full-path targets (a folder name followed by a page name) also resolve —
see "Clashing names" below. See [[Limitations]] for other current gaps
(embeds, inline-code-span safety).

## What "resolves" actually means

At each page's own render time, a Pandoc Lua filter looks up every
bracketed wikilink against that registry:

- **Found** → rewritten to a real link, and an edge is recorded for
  [[The Graph Widget]].
- **Not found** → left as plain, unlinked text (brackets included), and a
  warning is printed. Nothing else happens.

That second case is worth being explicit about: **a wikilink to a page
that doesn't exist does not create that page.** The registry is built once,
up front, only from pages already in the project. For example, this
paragraph links to [[This Page Does Not Exist Anywhere]], which isn't a
real page. It renders as inert text, and the build prints:

```
WARNING: unresolved wikilink [[This Page Does Not Exist Anywhere]] in wikilinks-and-aliases/index.qmd
```

To make broken links fail the *build* instead of just warning, pass
`--strict` to the pre-render script (edit the `pre-render` line in
`_extensions/quarto-graph/_extension.yml`); see [[CLI]].

## Excluding a page from the graph entirely

A project-wide `quarto-graph: exclude:` list in `_quarto.yml` removes
matching pages from the registry before it's built, a full opt-out, not
just hiding a node from [[The Graph Widget]]'s drawing. An excluded page is
never scanned, and a `[[wikilink]]` pointing at it comes back **unresolved**,
the same as a typo:

```yaml
quarto-graph:
  exclude:
    - archive/       # this directory and everything under it
    - "*.draft.qmd"  # glob pattern, matched against each page's project-relative path
```

A trailing `/` excludes a directory and everything under it; anything else
is a plain glob. This is quarto-graph's own list, independent of whether
Quarto itself renders the page: it's applied on top of the base file list,
which for a real Quarto project is Quarto's own fully-resolved `quarto
inspect` output (respecting a project's `project: render:` globs and
Quarto's default exclusions already), or a plain recursive scan for a bare
folder with no `_quarto.yml`.

## Plain Markdown links resolve too, but differently

A normal Markdown link, `[text](other.qmd)`, is also treated as an edge and
a backlink source, not just `[[wikilinks]]`. See [[Backlinks]] and
[[The Graph Widget]].

The resolution mechanism is different, though: a Markdown link resolves by
*path*, not by registry name lookup. The href is resolved relative to the
linking page's own path (or from the project root, for a leading `/`), and
must land on another page's real project path. That means none of the
wikilink conveniences apply:

- no case-insensitivity — the path has to match exactly
- no `also-known-as:` names — only the page's actual path resolves
- no heading-anchor slug rewriting — a `#fragment` is stripped and ignored,
  not resolved
- no display-text syntax — the link text is whatever you already wrote

An external URL, a protocol-relative href, or a path that doesn't match any
project page is left alone entirely. Unlike an unresolved wikilink, this
doesn't print a warning — a Markdown link to an asset, an external site, or
a typo'd path isn't necessarily a mistake. See [[Limitations]].

## Clashing names

If two pages register the same target name (two files sharing a stem in
different folders, two `index.qmd` pages sharing a folder name, two pages
with the same `also-known-as:`, and so on), the registry keeps only the
first one registered and prints:

```
WARNING: duplicate link target 'name' (first-page.qmd vs second-page.qmd); keeping first-page.qmd
```

A bare wikilink to that name always resolves to whichever page was kept —
but the other page is still reachable, by qualifying the target with enough
of its own folder path to be unique: `[[docs/api]]`,
`[[vendor/api]]`, or, for a folder note specifically, the fully spelled-out
`[[docs/api/index]]`. This applies to a `title:` collision too, not just a
stem or folder-name one. `also-known-as:` names don't get this treatment —
they're already a deliberately-chosen unique name, so give the other page
one of those instead if you'd rather not qualify the path.
